advisories.summary: Lodash versions 4.0.0 through 4.17.22 are vulnerable to prototype pollution via the _.unset and _.omit functions. An attacker can pass crafted paths to delete methods from global prototypes such as Object.prototype, though the issue only permits deletion and not overwriting of properties.

advisories.summary: Lodash 4.17.23 and earlier are vulnerable to a prototype pollution bypass in _.unset and _.omit. The fix for CVE-2025-13465 only guards against string key members, so attackers can bypass it by passing array-wrapped path segments to delete properties from built-in prototypes including Object.prototype, Number.prototype, and String.prototype.
advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: Lodash _.template is vulnerable to code injection via unsanitized options.imports key names. Untrusted key names are passed to the Function() constructor sink without validation, and the use of assignInWith (which enumerates inherited properties) also means that pre-existing prototype pollution on Object.prototype can flow into the Function() sink and execute arbitrary code at template compilation time.
advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: Handlebars is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via the @partial-block mechanism. When a helper with write access to the template data context overwrites @partial-block with a crafted Handlebars AST, subsequent invocation of that partial causes the runtime to dynamically compile the AST, executing arbitrary JavaScript on the server.
advisories.why: If attacker-controlled input reaches the affected feature, it may be interpreted as code instead of ordinary data.

advisories.summary: Handlebars has a time-of-check/time-of-use flaw in container.lookup() when the compat compile option is enabled. The function uses lookupProperty() as a security gate but then discards its result and performs a raw unguarded property access, bypassing prototype-access controls.
advisories.why: The upstream source reports a security issue affecting this version. Whether it can be exploited depends on how the affected feature handles untrusted input; check the advisory for details.

advisories.summary: Handlebars is vulnerable to Denial of Service via unregistered decorator syntax. When a template contains a decorator reference to an unregistered decorator (e.g. {{*n}}), the compiled template attempts to invoke undefined as a function, causing an unhandled TypeError that crashes the Node.js process.
advisories.why: Crafted input can consume excessive resources or crash the affected application. The impact depends on the feature and runtime used.

advisories.summary: Handlebars is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution through dynamic partial lookups. A crafted object with call: true placed in the template context bypasses resolvePartial() guards and causes the runtime to compile the object as a Handlebars AST via env.compile(), executing injected JavaScript on the server.
advisories.why: If attacker-controlled input reaches the affected feature, it may be interpreted as code instead of ordinary data.

advisories.summary: The Handlebars CLI precompiler is vulnerable to code injection through multiple unsanitized inputs: template file names, the namespace (-n), CommonJS path (-c), and AMD path (-h) options are all interpolated into generated JavaScript without escaping. An attacker who controls these values can inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes when the generated bundle is loaded.
advisories.why: If untrusted content reaches the affected feature, an attacker may run JavaScript in a visitor’s browser and act as that visitor.

advisories.summary: Handlebars has an asymmetric prototype method blocklist where __lookupSetter__ is omitted while its counterparts are blocked. advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: When Axios runs on Node.js and is given a data: scheme URL, it decodes the entire payload into memory and returns a synthetic 200 response, ignoring maxContentLength and maxBodyLength limits. An attacker can supply a very large data: URI to cause unbounded memory allocation and crash the process, constituting a Denial of Service.
advisories.why: Crafted input can consume excessive resources or crash the affected application. The impact depends on the feature and runtime used.

advisories.summary: The mergeConfig function in axios crashes with a TypeError when processing configuration objects containing __proto__ as an own property, such as those created via JSON.parse. An attacker who can pass a JSON payload with __proto__ as a config key can trigger a complete Denial of Service.
advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: Axios does not correctly normalize hostnames when checking NO_PROXY rules, causing requests to loopback addresses with a trailing dot (localhost.) or IPv6 literals ([::1]) to bypass NO_PROXY matching and be routed through the configured proxy. Attackers controlling request URLs can exploit this to bypass SSRF mitigations and reach sensitive loopback or internal services.
advisories.why: In affected server-side uses, an attacker may make the application send requests to unintended destinations, including private services.

advisories.summary: Axios is vulnerable to being used as a gadget in a prototype pollution attack chain: when Object.prototype is polluted with CRLF-containing header values via another dependency, Axios merges the polluted properties into request headers without sanitization. This allows HTTP request smuggling attacks including bypassing AWS IMDSv2 session token requirements to steal cloud credentials.
advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: Axios contains prototype pollution gadgets in request config processing; a polluted Object.prototype.transformResponse can be executed with access to request credentials and response data, enabling credential theft and response hijacking across all requests.
advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: Axios does not enforce maxBodyLength for stream request bodies when maxRedirects is set to 0, because the native HTTP transport path used in that configuration does not perform byte counting. Oversized streamed uploads are sent in full despite the configured body size limit, enabling uncontrolled upstream data transfer and potential resource exhaustion.
advisories.why: Crafted input can consume excessive resources or crash the affected application. The impact depends on the feature and runtime used.

advisories.summary: The toFormData helper in Axios recursively walks nested objects without a depth limit or try/catch protection. An attacker who can provide a deeply nested object as request data or params can trigger a stack overflow, crashing the Node.js request handler or process.
advisories.why: Crafted input can consume excessive resources or crash the affected application. The impact depends on the feature and runtime used.

advisories.summary: Axios is vulnerable to a prototype pollution gadget that allows header injection in the Node.js HTTP adapter. When Object.prototype is polluted with duck-typed FormData properties including getHeaders, Axios treats any plain object payload as a FormData instance and calls the attacker-controlled getHeaders() function, merging arbitrary headers into the outgoing request.
advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: The fix for the NO_PROXY hostname normalization bypass (GHSA-3p68-rc4w-qgx5) is incomplete: shouldBypassProxy() does not resolve loopback address equivalents. When NO_PROXY=localhost is set, requests to 127.0.0.1 and [::1] are still routed through the configured proxy, enabling SSRF bypasses against internal services.
advisories.why: In affected server-side uses, an attacker may make the application send requests to unintended destinations, including private services.

advisories.summary: Axios has multiple prototype pollution gadgets where config properties are read without hasOwnProperty guards. When Object.prototype is polluted by a co-dependency, an attacker can silently intercept and modify every JSON response (parseReviver gadget) or fully hijack the underlying HTTP transport to intercept credentials and headers (transport gadget).
advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: The Axios 1.15.0 patch for NO_PROXY hostname normalization is incomplete: the isLoopback() function only recognizes three specific addresses (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) but not the full RFC 1122 loopback subnet 127.0.0.0/8. Requests to any 127.x.x.x address other than 127.0.0.1 bypass NO_PROXY matching and are routed through the configured proxy, enabling SSRF.
advisories.why: In affected server-side uses, an attacker may make the application send requests to unintended destinations, including private services.

advisories.summary: Axios does not enforce maxContentLength when responseType is set to 'stream'. The response stream is returned directly without byte-counting, allowing unbounded downstream consumption of arbitrarily large server responses despite the configured limit.
advisories.why: Crafted input can consume excessive resources or crash the affected application. The impact depends on the feature and runtime used.

advisories.summary: Axios is vulnerable to a prototype pollution gadget via the validateStatus config property, which uniquely uses the JavaScript in operator (which traverses the prototype chain) during config merging. When Object.prototype.validateStatus is polluted with () => true, all HTTP error responses (401, 403, 500, etc.) are silently treated as successes, bypassing authentication and error handling.
advisories.why: Crafted input may change shared JavaScript object properties, causing unexpected behavior or bypassing checks in code that uses them.

advisories.summary: The encode() function in Axios's AxiosURLSearchParams helper contains a character map entry that reverses the safe percent-encoding of null bytes: '%00' is mapped back to a raw null byte '\x00' after encodeURIComponent has correctly encoded it. Applications using AxiosURLSearchParams directly without an external encoder will produce URLs containing raw null bytes, which can cause truncation or WAF bypass in downstream C-based parsers.
advisories.why: The upstream source reports a security issue affecting this version. Whether it can be exploited depends on how the affected feature handles untrusted input; check the advisory for details.

advisories.summary: Axios's XSRF token protection uses truthy/falsy semantics rather than strict boolean comparison for the withXSRFToken config property. When Object.prototype is polluted with any truthy non-boolean value for withXSRFToken, the same-origin check is bypassed and the XSRF token is sent to all cross-origin destinations, enabling CSRF attacks after token theft.
advisories.why: The upstream source reports a security issue affecting this version. Whether it can be exploited depends on how the affected feature handles untrusted input; check the advisory for details.

advisories.summary: Axios 1.15.2 exposes two prototype pollution gadgets: HTTP header injection via utils.merge() building plain objects that walk the prototype chain, and a crash DoS where a polluted Object.prototype.get or .set causes TypeError on every axios request.

When constructing per-part headers for binary or Blob-like values, value.type is interpolated without sanitizing CRLF sequences, allowing an attacker who controls the MIME type of an uploaded file to inject arbitrary headers into the multipart body.

advisories.summary: Axios is vulnerable to a prototype pollution gadget via the parseReviver configuration property. When Object.prototype.parseReviver is polluted, Axios uses the attacker-controlled function as a JSON.parse reviver on every response, enabling silent selective modification of JSON values (e.g. privilege escalation) and exfiltration of all response data including API keys.

advisories.summary: Axios has five config properties (auth, baseURL, socketPath, beforeRedirect, insecureHTTPParser) that are read from the merged config object without hasOwnProperty guards, making them exploitable as prototype pollution gadgets. When Object.prototype is polluted, these properties enable credential injection, request hijacking to attacker-controlled servers, SSRF via Unix sockets, and arbitrary code execution via redirect callbacks.

advisories.summary: DOMPurify 3.1.3 through 3.2.6 and 2.5.3 through 2.5.8 contain a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass attribute sanitization by exploiting missing textarea rawtext element validation in the SAFE_FOR_XML regex. Attackers can include closing rawtext tags like </textarea> in attribute values to break out of rawtext contexts and execute JavaScript when sanitized output is placed inside rawtext elements. The 3.x branch was fixed in 3.2.7; the 2.x branch was never patched.

advisories.summary: When USE_PROFILES is enabled, DOMPurify rebuilds ALLOWED_ATTR as a plain array whose properties are looked up by name, making it susceptible to prototype pollution. If Array.prototype has been polluted with an event handler attribute name (e.g. onclick), DOMPurify will allow that event handler to survive sanitization, resulting in DOM-based XSS.
advisories.why: If untrusted content reaches the affected feature, an attacker may run JavaScript in a visitor’s browser and act as that visitor.

advisories.summary: DOMPurify's ADD_ATTR predicate function mechanism (via EXTRA_ELEMENT_HANDLING.attributeCheck) short-circuits URI validation when the predicate returns true. This allows unsafe protocols such as javascript: to survive sanitization in href and similar attributes, enabling DOM-based XSS when such links are activated.
advisories.why: If untrusted content reaches the affected feature, an attacker may run JavaScript in a visitor’s browser and act as that visitor.

advisories.summary: DOMPurify is vulnerable to mutation-XSS (mXSS) when sanitized HTML is embedded into special raw-text wrapper elements such as xmp, script, iframe, noembed, noframes, or noscript before being assigned via innerHTML. Attacker-controlled sequences like </xmp> inside attribute values close the raw-text context during the second parse, causing the sanitized output to mutate into executable markup.
advisories.why: If untrusted content reaches the affected feature, an attacker may run JavaScript in a visitor’s browser and act as that visitor.

advisories.summary: DOMPurify has a logic inconsistency where FORBID_TAGS is not checked when a function-based ADD_TAGS (tagCheck) returns true. Due to short-circuit evaluation, the FORBID_TAGS check is never evaluated, allowing explicitly forbidden elements to pass through sanitization when EXTRA_ELEMENT_HANDLING.tagCheck is configured.
advisories.why: The upstream source reports a security issue affecting this version. Whether it can be exploited depends on how the affected feature handles untrusted input; check the advisory for details.

advisories.summary: DOMPurify has an asymmetric security inconsistency where FORBID_TAGS does not win over a function-based ADD_TAGS predicate, while FORBID_ATTR correctly wins over ADD_ATTR. When ADD_TAGS is provided as a function that returns true, explicitly forbidden tags such as iframe and form pass through sanitization with their attributes intact.
advisories.why: If untrusted content reaches the affected feature, an attacker may run JavaScript in a visitor’s browser and act as that visitor.

advisories.summary: DOMPurify's SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES feature fails to strip Mustache/template expressions when RETURN_DOM or RETURN_DOM_FRAGMENT is used. The final string-scrubbing pass that removes expressions like {{...}} is skipped in DOM-return mode, and split text nodes (e.g. from removed intermediate tags) can rejoin to form a complete expression that template-evaluating frameworks like Vue 2 will execute.
advisories.why: If untrusted content reaches the affected feature, an attacker may run JavaScript in a visitor’s browser and act as that visitor.

advisories.summary: DOMPurify versions 3.0.1 through 3.3.3 are vulnerable to an XSS bypass via prototype pollution. When no CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING is specified, the fallback plain object inherits from Object.prototype; if an attacker has polluted Object.prototype.tagNameCheck and Object.prototype.attributeNameCheck with permissive regexes, DOMPurify allows arbitrary custom elements with event handler attributes through sanitization.
